items.english: "You won't listen, will you." The young father looked hard at the small round arms and at the child's eyes with their rather dark, long lashes, moving quickly and brightly without a moment's pause, as if wondering what was to be done, and then, with a smile over his whole face, lightly pinching the round thrust-out cheek with his finger, he took a large bowl from under the table as if feeling for it and put it into her hand.
notes: I read 彼女の手 as the mother's hand: he hands her the large bowl for her to serve the rice in p8. The Japanese can also read as the child's hand; the passage leaves it soft, so I keep the plain 'her' and flag the doubt for the desk.

items.english: She served out the hot fresh-cooked rice, with white steam rising thick from the pot, and handed it to him. And her young large eyes too, full of a mother's gladness, gazed at the child, never still for an instant, lovely like a little bird. And as if she could bear it no longer, murmuring inwardly to herself whatever shall we do with this child, and looking for all the world as if she loved it beyond all help, she said firmly, "Baby," but the smile overflowed from her face, and she looked at the man's face as if asking for help. And the three of them, as if they had forgotten everything, smiled at one another as if to say what should they do for the child. And for the child they set about their meal with a warm bustle, and with smiles and gladness overflowing of themselves on top of it. And in the clattering bustle they did not hear the sound of the rain and wind.
notes: I keep 坊や as 'Baby' for a girl child, following the bible's policy for period generic use, rather than 'boy'; flagged for editor.
口のうちに独言 is an inward half-uttered murmur rather than spoken address; I keep it as murmuring inwardly to preserve the soft drift toward thought.

items.english: The young father kept his large red hand spread busily over the table. And his eyes, holding back the smile that welled up in spite of himself because of the child, steadied the child and put a little food into that small red mouth. In the gaps, hurriedly opening a wide mouth, he pushed rice into his own mouth.
